properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform. NOTE: an initial attempt also used the real, confirmed positions of the Sophie Maxwell Building and the UCSF Block 2 building as anchors, but they produced 50-60m of error against the street-only fit -- this diagram is dated Feb 26, 2020, predating UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as a life-science anchor tenant, so those two real buildings likely do not sit where this 2020 figure's own numbered blocks would place them (their own real parcels are used directly elsewhere in this dataset and were NOT re-derived from this diagram). The final transform here uses street intersections only. Residual error against those control points is roughly 8-24m. Traced polygons were additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels (and against Prequel Park's approximate geometry) so this speculative tracing never overrides real or better-sourced geometry. REBUILT 2026-09-16: this block was the one Potrero feature never re-transformed during this site's GDAL/TPS overhaul (see Block 1/3/4/etc.'s own digitization_method), and a user-flagged visual check (Humboldt Street Plaza appearing to sit 'east of Block 9' instead of between Block 4 and Block 9) traced back to Block 9 still using the old, less accurate transform -- it had drifted enough to overlap Block 4 (97 m2) after Block 4's own GDAL/TPS correction. Re-traced this block's actual notched building outline (10 vertices, following the real jogs in the diagram's own thin-line outline -- a stepped-out notch on the NE side, a stepped-in notch on the SW side) via programmatic black-pixel detection, then ran it through the same (GCP-corrected) TPS transform as the rest of the site. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D at default.sfplanning.org) is dead (404); the text above describes the final D4D (dated February 26, 2020), so source_doc_urls now points to potreropower_D4D_final.pdf, where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) with a scale bar (0-400 ft), a north arrow and the street labels listed above. The '~2023-24 arrival' of UCSF as anchor tenant, mentioned above, has no cited source; the dated source found is the UC Regents' September 2024 CEQA findings (Attachment 6), which state that in 2024 the City approved an assignment and assumption agreement under which UCSF assumes a portion of the developer's rights. The Sophie Maxwell / UCSF Block 2 anchor and clip steps are this project's own work, not a source claim. The accuracy_caveat's sentence about a possible overlap with the UCSF Block 2 area was removed: in the final D4D Block 2 and Block 9 are several blocks apart, and this polygon does not overlap the Block 2 parcel (4175027; about 114 m apart in the 2026-09-29 comparison). The final figure does place the Humboldt Street Plaza label between Blocks 4 and 9, and draws Block 9's outline as a 10-vertex notched Potential Build-To Line, as described above. The committed geometry was not changed.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built, and it is not vacant land: it is where the Unit 3 Power Block (partly demolished June 2023 to July 2024 per the 2024 annual compliance report) and the 300-ft Stack stand, and where the interim Prequel Park is planned. No Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St, about 21,900 sq m, recorded 2022-08-30), which also overlaps the Block 3 and Block 4 footprints. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (rebuilt 2026-09-16 via the site's GDAL/TPS pass -- see digitization_method), and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), not a lot of its own.
properties.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) permits Residential, Institutional, Retail (Hotel is permitted, note 10), Non-Retail Sales/Services (office, at the lowest floors only), Entertainment and limited PDR uses on Block 9, and not Laboratory or Life Science. Figure 6.2.3's 'Block 9 Building Configurations' inset shows two alternate massings, by its colour-coded labels: 'with Unit 3' 85 ft, 65 ft and 35 ft plus Unit 3 itself at about 130 ft ('~130''), and 'without Unit 3' 125 ft and 85 ft; the '177'MAX', '110'MAX' and '102'MAX' labels are tick-ended dimension lines, not heights, and Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 9 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft). This block's real-world area is where Unit 3 and the Stack physically stand (confirmed by the D4D's Standard 6.2.1 and the Chronicle, May 2025; the Stack is mapped separately, as potrero_the_stack) and where Prequel Park's approximate interim-park geometry sits (Port Commission memo 10A; also mapped separately, and excluded here via clipping) -- treat this polygon as the block's outer development envelope, not a claim that all of it is buildable independent of those other real features.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned': the hotel is approved, but the Chronicle (May 2025) reported its construction could be a decade away and an interim park is planned. Use 'mixed': Table 3.1.1 permits residential, hotel and other retail, office and entertainment uses on Block 9.
